answer: A bonded stake turns each identity into a costly signal: an agent must lock a refundable deposit on a public ledge before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Honest agents harbor their reputation in that single stake, earning it back over time, while a Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits and one detection wipes out the whole batch.
